comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose revenue performance for their primary server/data center product lines in 2024. Intel reports a modest $182 million increase in DCAI server revenue, driven by higher Average Selling Prices (ASPs) of 12% despite a 10% decrease in volume due to lower demand and competitive mix. In contrast, AMD reports a massive 94% increase in Data Center net revenue to $12.6 billion, driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs. While both companies attribute revenue changes to product mix and pricing dynamics, Intel's server segment saw volume declines, whereas AMD's server segment experienced substantial volume and revenue growth.

comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded segment net revenue and drivers for fiscal year 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Embedded net revenue decreased by 33% to $3.6 billion in 2024 from $5.3 billion in 2023, primarily due to lower demand as customers normalized inventory levels.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies address the impact of customer inventory normalization on segment revenues in 2024. Intel's Client Computing Group (CCG) notes that notebook volume increased 12% as customer inventory levels improved compared to the higher levels in 2023. Similarly, AMD's Embedded segment experienced a 33% revenue decrease primarily because 'customers continued to normalize their inventory levels.' Both disclosures highlight inventory correction as a key driver of volume and revenue fluctuations in their respective non-data-center segments.
